Layered construction. Lasting performance.

Better materials.
Better infrastructure.

Engineered in layers, with a purpose behind every one.

FRP means Fiber Reinforced Polymer. Fiberglass reinforcement, a high-strength resin matrix and a mineral-filled core work together to deliver rigidity and strength. The surface layers address weather exposure and grip; the reinforcing layers resist compression, tension and bending.

UV-stable top coating
Protects against sunlight, weathering and colour fade.
Anti-skid surface texture
A textured finish for pedestrian and vehicle grip.
Resin matrix binder
High-strength polymer resin binds the layers together.
Woven fiberglass reinforcement
Structural reinforcement to resist compression and cracking.
Filler-reinforced composite base
A mineral-filled core provides rigidity and impact strength.
Fiberglass mat — tension layer
Bottom reinforcement resists tensile and bending forces.

Illustration from our brochure. Layer proportions vary by size and load class.

Match the opening

Confirm the specification

A correct fit.
From the ground up.

Four installation principles from the brochure.
Confirm the detailed specification for your chosen cover.

  1. Prepare the bed

    Prepare the concrete bed to suit the height of the frame.

  2. Match the openings

    The frame’s clear opening should match the chamber’s clear opening.

  3. Support the frame

    Embed the frame in M-20 grade concrete. Confirm bedding dimensions with our team before installation.

  4. Align the surface

    Set the top of the frame level with the finished road or pavement surface.

Full support makes the difference.

Seat the frame fully on the concrete bed. Avoid unsupported overhangs and frames sitting above the finished surface. The brochure illustrates correct frame seating and cover, frame and mortar alignment.

Product resources

The details.
Ready when you need them.

Explore product formats, composite materials, load classes and installation guidance. Contact our team for details specific to your project.

What is an FRP composite cover?

FRP stands for Fiber Reinforced Polymer. Surazo’s brochure describes a layered construction using fiberglass, a polymer resin binder and a mineral-filled core, with a textured, UV-stable surface.

Which product formats are available?

The range includes circular and square manhole covers, slotted gully covers and frames, and modular trench cover sections for continuous drainage. Confirm the size, frame and load class with our team.

What information do I need for a quote?

Share the product type, clear opening or required size, load class and quantity. Include your project location and application so our team can help with the specification.

Can I request a custom size?

Yes. Custom sizes and load classes are available on request. Contact our team to discuss your requirements and confirm availability.

What should I check before installation?

Match the frame opening to the chamber, fully support the frame on the specified concrete bed, and align the top with the finished surface. Ask our team for the installation requirements for your selected cover.

Does the load class describe total vehicle weight?

The brochure illustrates that a vehicle’s weight is distributed across its wheels and axles. Gross vehicle weight alone is not enough to select a cover. Ask our team to confirm the load class and installation requirements for the actual traffic conditions; the brochure’s truck example is illustrative, not a vehicle-specific approval.

Where can I get technical documents?

Contact support@surazocovers.com for product-specific dimensions, load-class information and applicable test documentation.
